sentence_stem: If only I had studied harder,
correct_completion: I would have passed the exam.
full_sentence: If only I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
acceptable_variants: I could have passed the exam.
I might have passed the exam.

options.text: I would pass the exam tomorrow.
options.why_wrong: This describes a future possibility. The regret in the stem refers to the past, so the result must also be past (would have + past participle).

options.text: I did not study at all.
options.why_wrong: This is a simple past fact. It does not complete the unreal past result that 'if only' with the past perfect expects.

options.text: I will study harder next time.
options.why_wrong: This is a future promise, not the past regret expressed by 'if only' followed by the past perfect.

options.text: I would have passed the exam.

grammar_focus: Third conditional with 'if only' to express past regret
explanation: After 'if only' with the past perfect, the main clause needs would have followed by a past participle to express an unreal past result. Turkish speakers may use a simple past form here, because Turkish marks past and conditional meaning with suffixes rather than with a separate auxiliary structure like 'would have'.
translation: Keşke daha çok çalışsaydım, sınavı geçerdim.
